observations: The packaged CLI reaches DotNetConsoleGenerationInput only after an alpha artifact manifest supplies one binding revision, one consumer reference assembly revision, and a non-empty ordinal compilation reference closure.
The existing command service verifies and consumes exact Console inputs but owns no command that materializes shell, Open Console, binding, artifact-manifest, or compiler-reference closure bytes.
The current cold-proof script accepts a prebuilt ConsoleFixtureRoot, so it cannot prove that a package-only consumer can author the required product inputs.
JTest previously depended on a deleted consumer-specific JTest.HostInputs helper; recreating it would keep the product journey incomplete.
The generated Console host has one ProjectReference to one selected consumer project, and the current metadata inspector resolves binding-visible types only from that selected TargetRefPath assembly.

The existing design calls the selection a consumer project but does not make the single Console integration-project topology or the public per-command I<Command>Handler seam sufficiently discoverable; a pure contracts-only selection is not the current supported contract.

The existing shell-free process runner, strict serializers, schema modules, Console binding validators, metadata inspector, artifact resolver, and transactional filesystem boundary provide compatible implementation seams.
